_comment: Photo archive. To add a photo: copy a block, change the values. 'src' can be a full web address or a local path like assets/images/my-photo.jpg. 'decade' drives the decade filter — use a 4-digit decade (e.g. 1950) or 'unknown'. 'topic' drives the topic filter and must match one of the topics listed below. Topic names are shared with the Internet Archive listing in photos-ia.json, because the Photographs page puts both in one menu.

photos.title: Castro Street
photos.caption: Looking down downtown Mountain View's main street in the early 1950s, lined with neon signs and four lanes of traffic.

photos.title: Castro Street
photos.caption: Castro Street before the 1988–1990 downtown revitalization narrowed it to two lanes and widened the sidewalks.

photos.title: 201 Castro Street, then and now
photos.caption: A c. 1905 commercial building at 201 Castro Street compared with the same corner in the present day.

photos.title: Mountain View Station Depot
photos.caption: The Southern Pacific depot that gave New Mountain View its name. Demolished in 1959; a replica was built at Centennial Plaza in 2002.

photos.title: Castro Station
photos.caption: Castro Station looking north toward Rengstorff Avenue. Originally a flag stop granted to the Castro family in compensation for the railroad crossing their rancho.

photos.title: Mayfield Mall
photos.caption: One of the first fully enclosed, carpeted shopping malls in Northern California, at Central Expressway and San Antonio Road. Closed in 1983.

photos.title: The Historic Adobe Building
photos.caption: Built by New Deal work-relief laborers from adobe bricks made on site. Saved from demolition by the MVHA's Save the Adobe campaign and now on the National Register of Historic Places.

photos.title: The Adobe Building today
photos.caption: The restored Adobe Building at 157 Moffett Boulevard, home to most of the Association's quarterly meetings.

photos.title: The Rengstorff House
photos.caption: The oldest structure still standing in Mountain View, built by German immigrant Henry Rengstorff. Relocated to Shoreline Park and opened to the public in 1991.

photos.title: Moffett Field
photos.caption: Built on land granted in 1844 as Rancho Posolmi to Lope Yñigo, an Ohlone man. Local residents bought 1,000 acres and sold it to the Navy for one dollar.

photos.title: Hangar One
photos.caption: One of the world's largest freestanding structures, covering eight acres, built to house the airship USS Macon.

photos.title: The National Hotel
photos.caption: An early Mountain View hotel from the town's first decades as an incorporated city.

photos.title: Mountain View High School
photos.caption: The Castro Street campus of Mountain View Union High School, home of the Eagles. Demolished in 1987; the site is now Eagle Park, Park Place and City Centre.

photos.title: Mountain View city limit sign
photos.caption: A city limit sign from the decade when Mountain View's population and boundaries were expanding rapidly.

photos.title: Mountain View in 1954
photos.caption: Mountain View in the year the Historical Association was founded, as orchards began giving way to subdivisions.

photos.title: Richard McDonald and Daniel Burke, ice delivery
photos.caption: Delivering ice in Mountain View, a decade before mechanical refrigeration became common in local homes.

photos.title: Richard McDonald and Daniel Burke
photos.caption: Two Mountain View residents photographed in the year of the San Francisco earthquake.

photos.title: The Castro family adobe
photos.caption: Mariano Castro's house, which combined adobe and wood construction and featured a large west-facing porch. It replaced the smaller Estrada adobe of the early 1840s.

photos.title: Crisanto Castro
photos.caption: After his father Mariano's death in 1856, Crisanto Castro continued to live on the rancho with his widowed mother Maria Trinidad Peralta and his unmarried sisters.

photos.title: Francisca Armijo Castro
photos.caption: In 1857, Crisanto married Francisca Armijo. The couple and their children played a prominent role in the early development of Mountain View.

photos.title: Villa Lands of Mountain View
photos.caption: An 1876 map of the 'Villa Lands of Mountain View', showing parcels sold off from the Castro family's Rancho Pastoria de las Borregas.

photos.title: The Castro children at Villa Francisca
photos.caption: Susan Castro, Crisanto IV Castro, Mercedes Castro and, at back, Frank 'Pancho' Castro in front of Villa Francisca, built in 1911 and named in honour of their mother, Francisca.

photos.title: Five of the Castro children as adults
photos.caption: From left to right: Joe Castro, Susan Castro, Andrew Castro, Mercedes Castro, and Frank Castro.

photos.title: Dedication of the Castro Adobe historic marker
photos.caption: Reverend Father James Doyle and Mercedes Castro at the dedication of a placard marking the site of the first Estrada/Castro adobe, at Central Expressway and Rengstorff Avenue.

photos.title: Villa Francisca
photos.caption: The Castro family's Mission-style home shortly before a suspicious 1961 fire led the city to demolish it rather than repair the damage.

photos.title: Rengstorff Avenue
photos.caption: Rengstorff Avenue showing Rengstorff Park on the left and the Castro City neighbourhood on the right.

photos.title: A Mountain View residence
photos.caption: Postcard showing a Mountain View residence, believed to be in Castro City.

photos.title: Castro City Market
photos.caption: The Castro City Market and gas station, run by the Nakamura family, was a neighbourhood landmark until 1992. The building is now home to La Plaza Market.

photos.title: Escuela Avenue School
photos.caption: Now named Mariano Castro Elementary School. Renamed in 1959 after residents pointed out that 'Escuela Avenue School' translated to 'School Avenue School'.

photos.title: Rengstorff Park BBQ area
photos.caption: A group of mature eucalyptus and oak trees marks the spot where Villa Francisca once stood. The eucalyptus were likely planted by the Castro family.

photos.title: Interpretive sign at Rengstorff Park
photos.caption: A sign near the BBQ area describing the park's connection to the Castro family, including a small map of their rancho.

photos.title: An early MVHA meeting
photos.caption: An early meeting of the Mountain View Pioneer and Historical Association at the Adobe Building.

photos.title: Bob Gurr speaks at the MVHA summer BBQ
photos.caption: Original Disneyland Imagineer Bob Gurr speaks at the MVHA's 2016 summer BBQ at the Adobe Building, on his work with Mountain View's Arrow Development.

photos.title: MVHA board meeting at the History Center
photos.caption: Board members at the Mountain View History Center on the second floor of the Mountain View Public Library.

photos.title: MVHA at the Santa Clara County Fair
photos.caption: An Association volunteer staffing the MVHA exhibit at the Santa Clara County Fair.

photos.title: MVHA in the community
photos.caption: Association volunteers sharing Mountain View history at a local community event.

photos.title: The Eagle has landed
photos.caption: A bronze sculpture of an eagle mounted to the top of the new monument at Eagle Park, honouring the 1975 Mountain View High School CCS championship football team.

photos.title: Eagle monument dedication
photos.caption: MVHA President Pamela Baird welcomes the crowd gathered in Eagle Park for the dedication of the Mountain View High School monument.

photos.title: Interpretive sign at Eagle Park
photos.caption: The sign at the base of the eagle sculpture explains the history of Mountain View High School and how its 1975 football championship brought the city's diverse population together.

photos.title: Lloyd Lettis at 104
photos.caption: Lloyd Lettis, honoured by the MVHA as Mountain View's oldest living resident, at home in the house he bought for just under $13,000 in 1952.

photos.title: Lloyd Lettis
photos.caption: Lloyd Lettis laughs during a conversation at his home in Mountain View.

photos.title: A wall of family photos
photos.caption: A sparkling '104' sign sits on the counter underneath a wall of family photos in Lloyd Lettis's Mountain View home.
